title: Scalar trace base change on the second self-product projection
statement: Let l and p be primes, k a field of characteristic p distinct from l, and c either a finite subextension of the algebraic closure of Q_l or the closure coefficient. Let Y be a finite-type, quasi-compact, separated k-scheme. Write P=P1_Y and W=P×Y P. Assume Y,P,W are Noetherian and each has DiagonalTraceLocalizations l. Let family:Family l Y and reference:Reference l Y delta family be as in [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-reference]. For q:P1_Y→Y and its self-product W, put T=Lambda_P(1)[2] and beta=q*Rq*T→Rp2*(Lambda_W(1)[2]), the exchange followed by the first root-normalized shifted-line comparison of [lem-sfb-rational-p1-second-pretrace]. Then beta is invertible. Composing beta with the inverse secondDiagramPushIso, family.trace2, and the coefficient-unit isomorphism equals q* applied to trace_q followed by its coefficient-unit isomorphism, followed by the inverse unitator of the canonical monoidal derived q*. There is no arbitrary object K, counit, projection-factor contraction or diagonal insertion.

source.place: Second identity: trace base change, before tensoring with q*K and before integration.

proof.text: Invertibility of l on k gives invertibility on Y and P. Apply the existing completed Chern lifting theorem separately to the q and p2 presentations, obtaining two whole-system-normalized adjuncts. Their scalar images are the explicit independent maps of def-sfb-rational-p1-scalar-chern-maps.

Obtain the two invertible unit/Chern biproduct maps from scalar_chern_splittings. The zero trace values on the unit generators follow from negative Ext vanishing: their source is a single sheaf shifted by two and their target is a degree-zero sheaf. Prove the Chern degree-one values using scalar_chern_degree. Obtain the two generator equations for exchange from scalar_chern_base_change.

For any additive F and two binary splittings, the two generator equations give desc(Fu,Fc) beta = biprod.map(a,e) desc(u2,c2). The left splitting is inverse mapBiprod followed by F of the first splitting. Every other factor is invertible, so beta is invertible. Precompose the desired trace square with desc(Fu,Fc), cancel that isomorphism, and check on the two injections. The zero/one trace values prove the equations. Finally compose with singleUnitIso and unfold scalarUnitPullIso, which cancels its last inverse unit comparison.

theorem second_scalar_trace
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (c : Option (PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField l))
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] (hpl : p ≠ l)
    (Y : Scheme.{u}) [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsNoetherian Y] [IsNoetherian (ProjectiveLine Y)] [IsNoetherian (diagonalSurface Y)]
    [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l Y]
    [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l (ProjectiveLine Y)]
    [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l (diagonalSurface Y)]
    (δ : diagonalCompletedDomain l Y ⟶ diagonalCompletedCodomain l Y)
    (family : Family l Y) (_reference : Reference l Y δ family) :
    IsIso (secondTraceExchange l c k p hpl Y) ∧
      secondTraceExchange l c k p hpl Y ≫
        (secondDiagramPushIso (coefficient l c).X Y (line l c) (diagram l c Y family)).inv.app
          (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Modules (coefficient l c).X (diagonalSurface Y))
            0).obj (line l c (diagonalSurface Y))) ⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧) ≫
        (diagram l c Y family).trace₂ ≫
        (singleUnitIso (coefficient l c).X (ProjectiveLine Y)).hom =
      (moduleObjectDerivedPullback (coefficient l c).X (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y)).map
        (trace (coefficient l c).X Y (line l c) (diagram l c Y family) ≫
          (singleUnitIso (coefficient l c).X Y).hom) ≫
        (secondTraceUnitIso (coefficient l c).X Y).hom
